sources.title: AI capability is not the same as worker control
sources.observation: The synthesis separates access to AI capability from control over tasks, worker welfare, and successful remedy.
sources.mechanism: A tool can increase capability while decision rights, measurement, and correction remain with an employer or platform.
limits: This is a synthesis boundary, not a pooled causal estimate.

sources.title: Capability can arrive with dependence
sources.observation: The reader frames AI infrastructure as potentially building useful capability and dependence together, while keeping portability, exit, and state-control effects open.
sources.mechanism: A service can make work possible while increasing reliance on a provider or system that users cannot easily replace.
limits: The page preserves open questions about application migration, outcomes, portability, and exit.

sources.title: AI is changing which work remains scarce
sources.observation: The annual-report synthesis tracks AI as a force that can compress routine execution while increasing the value of distribution, judgment, accountability, and scarce expertise.
sources.mechanism: When routine work becomes cheap, value and bargaining power can move toward owners of distribution, context, judgment, and workflow control.
limits: This is a cross-company annual-report synthesis, not one company's measured AI outcome.

sources.title: AI can make routine execution cheaper while raising the value of strategy
sources.observation: The industry writeup describes AI website builders compressing template-based execution and shifting competition toward strategy, brand, personalization, and distribution.
sources.mechanism: Automation lowers the price of repeatable execution and can move scarce value toward higher-context work.
limits: The writeup combines industry estimates and company examples; each underlying measure needs source-level review before a general labor claim.

sources.title: AI demand creates a fast-growing infrastructure business
sources.observation: The Inc. 5000 record describes CoreWeave as a specialized GPU infrastructure provider serving AI labs, startups, and enterprises facing a shortage of compute.
sources.mechanism: A physical and financial infrastructure bottleneck can create a specialized layer that captures demand before AI becomes an ordinary workflow.
limits: The Inc. record identifies a growth hypothesis and revenue band; it does not prove customer benefit, durable margins, or AI productivity.

sources.title: Luma Optics sells the network layer needed by larger AI systems
sources.observation: The Inc. 5000 record describes Luma Optics as a maker of optical transceiver hardware for data centers handling demanding AI workloads.
sources.mechanism: As model workloads grow, the bottleneck can move from computing chips to the network that moves data between them, creating a specialized supplier layer.
limits: The Inc. record describes the business and growth, but does not prove customer performance, deployment durability, pricing power, or worker outcomes.

sources.title: Caylent sells help turning AI plans into cloud systems
sources.observation: The Inc. 5000 record describes Caylent as an AWS-focused services company using an AI-enabled delivery approach to help enterprises deploy ideas.
sources.mechanism: When enterprises cannot turn a model or cloud plan into a working system, implementation firms capture value by supplying scarce technical knowledge and execution capacity.
limits: The Inc. record identifies a service and growth story, but does not establish deployment quality, customer savings, worker workload, or repeatable AI productivity.

sources.title: Insurify applies AI to a consumer insurance choice
sources.observation: The Inc. 5000 record describes Insurify as an AI-powered insurance comparison platform that helps shoppers compare policies and quotes.
sources.mechanism: A comparison service can reduce search effort for consumers while also shaping which choices, prices, and explanations they see.
limits: The Inc. record does not show quote accuracy, consumer savings, recommendation bias, coverage quality, or how users can correct an error.

sources.title: VeraData uses AI to help nonprofits decide whom to approach
sources.observation: The Inc. 5000 record describes VeraData as an AI and machine-learning company serving philanthropic organizations with donor analysis.
sources.mechanism: Prediction tools can make scarce fundraising staff more selective while moving judgment about who receives attention into a data system.
limits: The Inc. record does not measure prediction accuracy, donor treatment, fundraising results, access effects, or how staff challenge a recommendation.

sources.title: AI work narratives need independent cultural measures
sources.observation: The Atlas thread places company-reported AI adoption beside editorial context, consumer measures, independent workplace measures, and an explicit open question about productivity and adoption.
sources.mechanism: A company narrative becomes more useful when it is compared with independent measures rather than treated as proof of an outcome.
limits: The thread explicitly says its sources do not establish productivity change, adoption scale, or causality.

sources.sourceLocator: FY2025 10-K and FY2026 Q1-Q3 direct SEC records
sources.title: C3.ai's report window shows what company records can and cannot prove
sources.observation: C3.ai's direct-record ledger covers the FY2025 10-K and three FY2026 10-Qs. It supports reported software, customer, accounting, deployment, risk, and financial facts, but does not independently measure accuracy, productivity, decision quality, privacy, worker conditions, or end-user outcomes.
sources.mechanism: A company's annual and quarterly reports can show commercial movement and stated deployments while leaving the lived result of an AI workflow unmeasured.
sources.reportingPeriod: FY2025 annual report plus FY2026 Q1, Q2, and Q3
limits: The report window does not identify an organization, model version, affected person, decision, input, output, error, override, appeal, remedy, or later outcome.

sources.sourceLocator: FY2025 annual and FY2026 Q1-Q3 accounting bridge
sources.title: NVIDIA's filings show platform growth without a measured deployment outcome
sources.observation: The NVIDIA bridge records an annual base and three subsequent quarters covering company revenue, data-center activity, supply, capacity, and export-control disclosures.
sources.mechanism: Infrastructure revenue can rise before a customer workload, worker result, or public benefit is measured.
sources.reportingPeriod: FY2025 annual report plus FY2026 Q1, Q2, and Q3
limits: The bridge does not establish customer workload value, switching cost, deployment return, worker outcome, or downstream public benefit.

reportWindow.reading: This is an issuer-reported platform and capacity history, not a customer or worker outcome.

sources.sourceLocator: FY2025 annual and FY2026 Q1-Q3 accounting bridge
sources.title: Microsoft's cloud growth does not identify the workload result
sources.observation: The Microsoft bridge records three quarters of reported revenue growth, Microsoft Cloud revenue, and commercial remaining performance obligations after the FY2025 annual report.
sources.mechanism: Cloud scale and contracted obligations can expand while price, use, capacity, reliability, and user benefit remain unresolved.
sources.reportingPeriod: FY2025 annual report plus FY2026 Q1, Q2, and Q3
limits: The bridge does not isolate AI contribution, workload use, customer value, reliability, affordability, energy effects, or worker outcomes.

reportWindow.reading: This is reported cloud growth and contract context, not proof of a customer workload result.

sources.sourceLocator: FY2025 annual and FY2026 Q1-Q3 accounting bridge
sources.title: Oracle's quarterly revenue movement leaves the operating cause open
sources.observation: The Oracle bridge records three reported quarterly revenue changes after the FY2025 annual report while explicitly leaving price, use, customer, capacity, AI demand, and outcome attribution unresolved.
sources.mechanism: Reported revenue can move without identifying the workload, capacity, contract, or user change that produced it.
sources.reportingPeriod: FY2025 annual report plus FY2026 Q1, Q2, and Q3
limits: The bridge does not establish AI demand, cloud capacity return, customer value, durability, or public and worker outcomes.

reportWindow.reading: This is a reported revenue sequence; the operating cause and outcome remain open.

sources.sourceLocator: FY2025 annual and FY2026 Q1-Q3 accounting bridge
sources.title: Broadcom's platform records need a separate customer-result test
sources.observation: The Broadcom bridge records three subsequent change windows and names unresolved price, unit, mix, integration, customer value, reliability, security, and AI-demand questions.
sources.mechanism: A supplier can report commercial movement while the customer workflow, integration cost, and downstream result remain unmeasured.
sources.reportingPeriod: FY2025 annual report plus FY2026 Q1, Q2, and Q3
limits: The bridge does not prove AI-demand durability, customer switching cost, deployment reliability, security, worker conditions, or public outcomes.

reportWindow.reading: This is a company-reported platform history; customer value and downstream effects need separate evidence.

sources.sourceLocator: AI user control and trust comparison
sources.title: Reported AI productivity is more common than reported control
sources.observation: A weighted Census HTOPS comparison reports AI use for at least one measured task at 54.948%, while 42.493% of AI users reported greater productivity, 21.736% reported control over when they used AI, and 10.995% reported control over how their data was used.
sources.mechanism: Perceived usefulness can spread faster than people’s reported control over the system or their data.
sources.unit: AI users and weighted survey respondents
sources.denominator: Census HTOPS June 2025 measures; weighted shares
limits: This is a cross-sectional descriptive comparison, not a causal estimate or proof that AI caused a change in autonomy or wellbeing.

sources.sourceLocator: direct evidence and task-level adoption comparison
sources.title: AI exposure does not tell us which workers adopt it
sources.observation: The NBER W35677 audit reports generative AI exposure across more than 80% of occupations and over 40% of tasks, while adoption within most occupations remains below half and no task exceeds 70% adoption.
sources.mechanism: Technical exposure becomes worker use only through access, training, permission, task fit, privacy, and perceived value.
sources.denominator: 13,920 employed RPS respondents and 55,634 person-task observations
limits: The study does not observe employer decision rights, downstream pay, wellbeing, control, or worker outcomes, and the working paper is not a randomized workplace experiment.

sources.title: AI access can change the time boundary of work before task structure
sources.observation: A randomized field experiment across 66 firms and 7,137 knowledge workers provided some workers access to an integrated generative-AI tool. Treated workers used less email time and worked less outside regular hours, while individual-level task quantity and composition did not detectably change in the study window.
sources.mechanism: Access to an AI tool can change when work is done before it changes who controls the work, how tasks are assigned, or where saved time goes.
sources.unit: worker-week digital activity and task measures
sources.denominator: 7,137 knowledge workers across 66 firms; randomized access with user and assignment estimands kept separate
limits: The study does not observe manager reallocation, performance targets, pay, promotion, health, household time, refusal, appeal, correction, or exit, and the six-month result is not a long-run organizational outcome.

sources.title: Some forms of algorithmic management are associated with less discretion and more stress
sources.observation: The JRC AIM-WORK survey and analysis cover 70,316 people across the EU and report associations between algorithmic management practices, lower autonomy, reduced ability to take breaks, greater work intensity, and work-related stress; the size and direction vary by practice.
sources.mechanism: Automated direction, monitoring, or pace-setting can change discretion and work intensity even when the specific vendor or system is not identified.
sources.unit: working-age individual workers across 27 EU Member States
sources.denominator: 70,316 survey respondents; paid-work routing applies to the main work block
limits: This is weighted cross-sectional survey and association evidence; it does not identify a single cause, vendor, employer, or matched before-and-after workplace.

sources.sourceLocator: five named workplace system stage comparison
sources.title: Named workplace systems reach governance and remedy stages before lived outcomes are measured
sources.observation: A five-case ledger follows IBM Germany AI systems, Microsoft Places and Copilot, OpenAI/Statsig recruitment systems, and Apple recruitment systems through named owners, dated rules, worker voice, control changes, enforcement or remedy, and the remaining worker, household, and exit gaps.
sources.mechanism: A named system can acquire formal governance, consent, correction, or monetary-remedy rules without producing a measured worker-level or household outcome.
sources.denominator: Five committed local records; cases retain their own evidence boundaries and are not pooled estimates
limits: The ledger is a bounded stage comparison, not a common workplace panel or causal estimate; most cases do not observe actual exposure, enforcement, worker welfare, household security, or practical exit.

sources.sourceLocator: adjudicated deactivation, restoration, and lost-remuneration chain
sources.title: A complete individual remedy chain can exist without proving system-wide repair
sources.observation: In one Amazon Flex case, a worker response and request for human discussion were followed by an adjudicated finding that review and evidence were inadequate, an order to reinstate access, and a separate order for $12,126.31 in lost remuneration.
sources.mechanism: A correction route matters only when a response is considered, the decision is revisited, access is restored, and lost income is addressed.
sources.denominator: One Amazon Flex worker with approximately 22,000 deliveries
limits: The orders establish a case-specific remedy, not payment receipt, durable access, recurrence prevention, anti-retaliation, or prevalence across Amazon or platform work.

sources.title: Human review can end in a compliant dismissal rather than restoration
sources.observation: In a separate Uber Eats case, the Commission found that a human Community Operations member considered the worker’s response and that the deactivation was compliant; the application was dismissed and no reactivation, pay, or compensation was ordered.
sources.mechanism: The presence of a human reviewer does not by itself determine whether a worker receives restoration; process, evidence, rule clarity, and the final disposition must be examined together.
sources.denominator: One Uber Eats worker; 97–98% of Brisbane partners reportedly met the rating threshold in the decision’s context
limits: This counterexample does not prove ratings are accurate, that all workers receive equivalent review, or that unrecorded correction did not occur.

outcomeBridges.title: Company movement versus worker control and remedy
outcomeBridges.question: Does reported AI capability or deployment movement produce more worker control, usable correction, and durable remedy?
canSupport: Company reports show commercial and operational movement.
Independent records show measured control, adoption, working-condition, governance, or remedy observations.
W33795 provides randomized evidence from tool access to short-run worker time patterns.
The named-system ledger shows that formal governance and reported remedies are distinct from lived outcomes.
The counterexample shows that human review does not guarantee restoration.
cannotSupport: W33795 does not connect to one of the five public companies or establish that their reported movement caused the worker result.
The evidence does not yet follow the same worker and workplace from access through correction, reallocation, and later result.
outcomeBridges.nextTest: Join the W33795-style access event to a workplace rule and later outcome: tool access → time/task change → manager reallocation or evaluation rule → worker discretion/pace → pay, health, family time, appeal, or exit.

insight.title: AI can return time without returning control
insight.plainLanguageSummary: The current evidence supports a narrower reading than 'AI makes work more productive': AI can remove visible tasks while decisions, measurement, correction, and dependence remain controlled by an employer, platform, or infrastructure provider.
insight.strongestAlternative: The apparent control gap may be temporary because early deployments have not yet matured into stable workflow changes.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A compatible longitudinal study shows durable control, pay, and remedy improvements for affected workers.
Company and independent records show that workers can understand, correct, and leave AI-mediated decisions without material penalty.
insight.nextTest: Track one named AI-mediated workflow from company deployment through worker or customer use, correction, appeal, and exit evidence.

additionalInsights.title: AI demand is building specialist layers before results are clear
additionalInsights.plainLanguageSummary: The current records show AI-related businesses appearing at several layers—compute, networking, implementation, comparison, and fundraising tools—while the customer result is still mostly unmeasured. This supports a map of where activity is forming, not a claim that the activity creates value.
additionalInsights.strongestAlternative: The apparent specialist-layer pattern may mostly reflect how the Inc. 5000 and industry sources classify growing companies, rather than a durable change in how customers buy or use AI.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Independent customer records show that these specialist services persist after initial experimentation and produce repeatable, measurable results.
Longitudinal evidence shows customers can compare, correct, replace, or exit these systems without material loss of control.
The businesses lose their distinct role as general-purpose platforms absorb the work without reducing customer choice or increasing dependence.
additionalInsights.nextTest: For one named customer workflow, trace the supplier, implementation step, actual use, correction path, switching option, and later result across at least two reporting periods.
